title: Lesson 10: Let Love Be Genuine
description: Romans 12 shows what real love looks like when it comes down from God, goes back up to Him, and reaches out to everyone around you, even enemies. This final lesson looks back at what God has done in you and looks ahead to the people He is sending you to.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you saw who God puts beside you in His mission, from your own church to the ends of the earth. This is the last lesson of Growing Together. It looks back at what God has done in you, and it looks ahead to what He wants to do through you. It begins with a strange feast.

blocks.title: A Table for Enemies
blocks.text:
The king of Syria was at war with Israel, and every time he set a trap, the prophet Elisha warned Israel's king where the raiders were waiting. So the king of Syria sent horses, chariots, and a great army by night to surround the town where Elisha was staying.

In the morning, Elisha's servant saw the army and panicked. Elisha prayed, and God opened the servant's eyes to see the hills full of horses and chariots of fire. Then God struck the soldiers with blindness, and Elisha led the whole army into Samaria, right into the hands of Israel's king.

The king could hardly believe it. "My father, shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down?" (2 Kings 6:21). Elisha told him no:

"Set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink and go to their master." So he prepared for them a great feast, and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away... And the Syrians did not come again on raids into the land of Israel. (2 Kings 6:22-23)

The enemy came to capture. They went home full. The raids stopped at a dinner table.

Centuries later, Paul pointed to the same kind of table: "If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink" (Romans 12:20). That kind of love does not start with you. It starts with a God who set a table for you while you were still His enemy (Romans 5:10). You love because He first loved you.
The Marks of Genuine Love

Paul spent eleven chapters of Romans on what God has done in Jesus. Then he turned to what that grace looks like in a real life, and he began with four words: let love be genuine. Genuine love is love without a mask, not a performance for others to watch.

Let love be genuine. Abhor what is evil; hold fast to what is good. Love one another with brotherly affection. Outdo one another in showing honor. Do not be slothful in zeal, be fervent in spirit, serve the Lord. Rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, be constant in prayer. Contribute to the needs of the saints and seek to show hospitality. Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse them. Rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep. Live in harmony with one another. Do not be haughty, but associate with the lowly. Never be wise in your own sight. Repay no one evil for evil, but give thought to do what is honorable in the sight of all. If possible, so far as it depends on you, live peaceably with all. Beloved, never avenge yourselves, but leave it to the wrath of God, for it is written, "Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord." To the contrary, "if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink; for by so doing you will heap burning coals on his head." Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
These marks follow the same shape as the Greatest Commandment you met at the start of Growing Deep.

Up toward God. "Be fervent in spirit, serve the Lord. Rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, be constant in prayer" (Romans 12:11-12). Genuine love starts with a heart kept warm by God. Growing Deep was about this: receiving His love and loving Him back.

Toward your family in Christ. "Love one another with brotherly affection. Outdo one another in showing honor... seek to show hospitality" (Romans 12:10, 13). Genuine love makes a home and a church where people belong. Growing Up was about this: loving your family and your church family.

Out toward everyone, even enemies. "Bless those who persecute you... live peaceably with all... overcome evil with good" (Romans 12:14, 18, 21). Genuine love does not stop with the people who love you back. Growing Out was about this: blessing your neighbors, your city, and the nations.

Some of these words may show you how much you still need to grow. Jesus stays with you in that growth. His Spirit helps you forgive, welcome, serve, and love when it is hard. These are the marks of His life taking shape in yours.

Elisha's servant saw an enemy army. God opened his eyes to see that they were not alone. Later, when Israel's king saw enemies he could destroy, Elisha called him to set a table for them. Ask God to help you see the people in front of you through His love. The person you would rather avoid may be someone He is calling you to bless. You do not have to know how they will respond to take the next loving step.
Disciples Who Make Disciples

Genuine love does not stay in a classroom. Jesus did not ask you to finish a course. He sent you to make disciples who make disciples (Matthew 28:19-20). Someone walked with you through these lessons. Now you get to walk with someone else.

You have learned to BLESS the people God has placed around you: begin with prayer, listen, eat, serve, and share your story. That is how a life of blessing starts at your own table and moves outward, to your neighborhood, your city, and the nations (Acts 1:8).
10.1 - Who is your one, and what are you excited to see God doing in them?
Look Back at What God Has Done

God has been at work in you through these courses, often in ways you could not see at the time. Looking back is one way to thank Him. The same cross shape helps you look back: up toward God, toward your home and your church, and out toward your neighbors.
10.2 - What are three ways God has grown you through Growing Together? Describe what has changed and where you see it in everyday life.
10.3 - What was your highlight of the whole Growing Together series?
What Is Next

Growing Together was never meant to be a finish line. Keep walking with the people who walked with you, and keep walking with your one. Keep the rhythms you have learned: God's Word, prayer, your church family, and a life of blessing. And when you are ready to help others lead, the next course, Leading in Discipleship, is on its way.
10.4 - Who could you begin Growing Together with, and how could you invite them?
Love Comes Down, Goes Up, and Reaches Out
The first lesson of Growing Deep asked which commandment matters most. Jesus' answer is where Growing Together ends.

"And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength." The second is this: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself." There is no other commandment greater than these.

God's love came down to you first. Your love goes back up to Him. And that same love reaches out, to your home, your church, your neighbors, and the nations. Love comes down, goes up, and reaches out.
This Week's Practice
Share your highlight from the series with the person who walked with you, and thank them. Then set a time to meet with your one.
Lesson 10 Review

Growing Deep began with a Father running toward His wayward son. You have spent these courses learning how deeply you are loved. Now that same love reaches through you toward others, even enemies. Jesus stays beside you as you learn to live His way. One of the joys of following Him is getting to share that life with someone else. Keep loving, keep sharing the good news, and help another person follow Jesus.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
